extracted.intended_audience: New York state agency rulemaking staff and officials responsible for preparing and filing rulemaking notices, regulatory agendas, RFAs, JISs, guidance document lists, and five-year reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for New York State agencies to prepare and publish Regulatory Agendas, five‑year rule reviews, guidance document listings, emergency adoptions, Regulatory Flexibility Analyses (RFAs), Job Impact Statements (JISs), and related notices and filings under SAPA and Executive Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda publication requirement (who must publish)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Housing and Community Renewal; Workers’ Compensation Board; departments of Agriculture and Markets, Education, Environmental Conservation, Financial Services, Health, Labor, Motor Vehicles and State; and the offices of Children and Family Services, and Temporary and Disability Assistance must publish semi-annual Regulatory Agendas in the State Register. An agency specified by the Governor or the Governor’s designee may be required to publish a Regulatory Agenda. Any agency may publish a Regulatory Agenda at its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandated agencies must publish semi-annually; other agencies may do so voluntarily or if directed by the Governor/designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Regulatory Agenda must include a list and brief description of the subject matter of all rules being considered for rule making and the name, public office, address and telephone number (and may provide an e-mail address) of the agency representative knowledgeable about the rule making, from whom information may be obtained and to whom comments may be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must also identify each rule described for which a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis or Rural Area Flexibility Analysis may be required, and provide outreach to potentially affected small businesses, local governments, and/or public or private interest located in rural areas for these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda format and submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Agenda text must be typed in the prescribed format in a Word or WordPerfect document and e‑mailed to NYSRegister@dos.ny.gov. Type 'Regulatory Agenda' in the subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publishing on an agency website is feasible, publish there as well. Agencies maintaining continuously updated Regulatory Agendas have special notification requirements (see continuous update criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda publication schedule and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Agendas are published twice a year: they must appear in the first January and the last June issue of the State Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines vary year-to-year; at latest have agenda ready around mid-December for January issue and mid-June for June issue. Submissions are accepted during the three submission weeks prior to the issue deadline. Refer to each year’s State Register Submission Deadlines on DOS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda website posting and continuously updated agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies which publish a Regulatory Agenda shall publish it on their respective websites whenever feasible. An agency that publishes its Regulatory Agenda on its website may maintain a continuously updated Regulatory Agenda, wherein a description of a rule is added when the agency begins to consider proposing it and is removed when the agency is no longer considering proposing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such descriptions must identify the date first listed and conspicuously indicate that the description has been newly listed for not less than 30 days after such date. Agencies maintaining continuously updated agendas need not publish a Regulatory Agenda in the last regular issue of the State Register in June; the January agenda must inform the public about the website and list addresses. The information must be republished in the last regular June issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to send Regulatory Agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Agendas should be e‑mailed (preferable), mailed or hand-delivered to Department of State, Division of Administrative Rules, One Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, Suite 650, Albany, NY 12231-0001, email: nysregister@dos.ny.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-mail is preferred; follow the prescribed format and subject line instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑year review requirement for existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by law, any rule adopted on or after January 1, 1997 shall be reviewed after five years and, thereafter, at five‑year intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency shall submit for publication in the January regulatory agenda a list of rules to be reviewed in the ensuing calendar year and provide an analysis of the need for and legal basis of the rule, invite public comment on continuation or modification, and indicate a last date for comments not less than 45 days from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑year review outcomes and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency determines a rule should be modified, it shall publish a notice of proposed rule making including a statement setting forth a reasoned justification for modification and an assessment of public comments prepared in accordance with subdivision four‑a of section 202 of SAPA. If it determines a rule should continue without modification, it shall publish a notice identifying the rule and statutory authority and include a statement setting forth a reasoned justification for continuation and an assessment of public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, include discussion of the degree to which changes in technology, economic conditions or other factors necessitate changes. For publication purposes, do not combine the Rule Review Notice with the Regulatory Agenda; they are separate notices published in separate sections of the Register. This five‑year review provision does not apply to consensus rules. Rule Review submissions may be e‑mailed; hard copy not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents annual listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Not less than once each year, every agency shall submit to the Secretary of State for publication in the State Register a list of all guidance documents on which the agency currently relies and provide information on where and how regulated parties and members of the public may inspect and obtain copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may make such documents available as provided in FOIL and may charge fees pursuant to that law for copies. If agency posts full text of all guidance documents on its website, the Secretary of State may exempt the agency from publication requirements (see certification criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance documents exemption and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State may exempt an agency from compliance with guidance document publication requirements upon determining the agency has published the full text of all guidance documents on its website. The Secretary shall publish a notice of such determination identifying the website in the State Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming exemption, agency must submit a certification to the Secretary of State claiming exemption and identifying website location(s) where full text is located. Form available on DOS website. A one‑year exemption certification must be signed by the agency head and submitted in hard copy. If list is available on website, use Guidance Document Certification form and choose item A; form can be uploaded or e‑mailed and signature is not required in that case. If submitting a list for publication, e‑mail the list (Word/WordPerfect) to nysregister@dos.ny.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑year review of guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Not less than once every five years, every agency shall conduct a process for reviewing and updating all guidance documents on which it currently relies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In conducting the process, the agency shall obtain feedback from regulated parties and members of the public who are directly or indirectly affected by the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus rule treatment and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A consensus rule (defined in SAPA) proposed for adoption on an expedited basis — because no person is likely to object as it repeals inapplicable provisions, conforms to nondiscretionary statutes, or makes technical/noncontroversial changes — is exempt from RIS, RFA, and RAFA requirements, but a JIS is still required. There is no exemption from submitting a JIS for a consensus rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must include a statement setting forth a clear and concise explanation of the basis for the agency’s determination that no person is likely to object. If any comment contains an objection, you must withdraw the notice. No rule defined as a 'major change' by Public Service Law may be adopted as a consensus rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency adoption authority and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency finds immediate adoption of a rule is necessary for preservation of public health, safety or general welfare and compliance with §202(1) would be contrary to public interest, the agency may dispense with all or part of those requirements and adopt a rule on an emergency basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed emergency adoption notice form. You must attach an RIS, RFA, RAFA and/or a JIS OR a statement indicating one will be published in the State Register within 30 days of the effective date of the emergency rule. A combined prescribed form exists to simultaneously advertise emergency adoption and propose a new rule or amendment/repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule duration limits and re‑adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided in law, an emergency rule cannot be effective for more than 90 days after being filed with the Secretary of State unless within that time the agency completes the regular rulemaking process. If re‑adopted prior to expiration, re‑adoptions will remain in effect for no longer than 60 days. Certain emergency rules (security authorizations, corporate/financial structures) may not expire if statute does not require public hearing and agency finds purpose would be frustrated by subsequent notice procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track expiration and re‑adoption timing carefully; ensure compliance with follow‑up publication obligations for required analytic statements when attaching 'to follow' statements at emergency adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and public availability of rulemaking materials
rubrics_metrics.description: You must transmit any rulemaking notice with the full text of the rule, RIS, RFA (including copies of any analysis and findings), RAFA, or revisions and any other information submitted to DOS to the Governor, Temporary President of the Senate, Speaker of the Assembly, Administrative Regulations Review Commission and the Regulatory Review Unit at the same time you submit your notice to DOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must make a copy of the complete text of the rule and all ancillary statements available to the public at the same time you submit your notice and send a copy to any person upon written request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification list maintenance and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must notify every person who has submitted a written request for notification of all rule makings. Such requests expire December 31 each year and must be renewed on or after December 1 for the succeeding year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may charge any person requesting a notice a fee consisting of the cost of preparation, handling and postage. Photocopies of any code, rule or regulation must be made available to the public upon payment of a fee not to exceed 25¢ per page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period minimums and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must accept public comment for, and must not schedule any public hearing that is required by statute until, at least 45 days after the notice of proposed rule making is published in the Register unless a different time is specified by statute. A notice must include the last date for submission of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Register is published weekly (Wednesday), the 45‑day period always expires on a Saturday; agencies must accept comments through close of business the following Monday (or next business day if Monday a holiday). Notices of revised rule making must also include a last date for submission. When an electronic mail address is provided for comments, DOS shall provide a direct link from the electronic State Register to that address to permit immediate electronic submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA) substantive requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule, agencies must consider approaches to accomplish statutory objectives while minimizing adverse economic impact on small businesses or local governments, including differing compliance/reporting requirements or timetables, use of performance rather than design standards, and whole or partial rule exemptions that do not endanger public health, safety or welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For §102(2)(a)(i) rules the RFA must: (a) describe the types and estimate the number of small businesses and local governments to which the rule will apply; (b) describe any reporting, recordkeeping and other compliance requirements and professional services needed; (c) estimate any costs to implement and continue to comply; (d) provide an assessment of the economic and technological feasibility of compliance by small businesses and local governments; (e) indicate how the rule was designed to minimize adverse economic impacts; (f) describe how the agency ensured participation of small businesses and local governments in developing the rule; and (g) if applicable, explain why no cure period is included for rules that establish or modify violations or penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFA procedural and scope rules (consolidation, exemptions, participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantifiable or numerical descriptions are allowed in an RFA, or more general descriptive statements if quantification is not practicable. A consolidated RFA may be submitted for a series of closely related rules. '(a)(ii)' rules and rules that do not impose adverse economic impacts or recordkeeping compliance requirements on small businesses or local governments are exempt from the RFA requirement; agency must provide statement of findings and reasons for that determination. An RFA is not required for a consensus rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must assure that small businesses and local governments had opportunity to participate via publication in appropriate publications, direct notification of interested parties, special open conferences, or adoption/modification of agency procedural rules to reduce cost/complexity of participation. Submit a revised RFA when the information is inadequate or incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job Impact Statement (JIS) substantive and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule, agencies must strive to accomplish statutory objectives in a manner that minimizes unnecessary adverse impacts on existing jobs and promotes development of new employment opportunities for residents of the state. For '(a)(i)' rules the elements required to be in a JIS must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available information is insufficient to determine whether a rule will have a substantial adverse impact on jobs, you may publish a statement soliciting needed information. A consolidated JIS may be submitted for closely related rules. You must submit a Revised JIS when the original is inadequate, substantial revisions necessitate modification, or new information allows a more complete evaluation. A 2,000‑word limit applies to JISs and revised JISs. If after soliciting information you still cannot determine impact, you may adopt the rule but must submit a Revised JIS including measures taken to evaluate potential impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference (identification and distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time material incorporated by reference is filed with DOS, you must transmit a copy (except a U.S. statute or code, CFR/Federal Register material or material readily available online free of charge — provide URL) to the Legislative Library and four designated Supreme Court Law Libraries. No amendment to any material incorporated by reference shall become effective unless adopted and filed with DOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of State may exclude incorporated material from the printed NYCRR. Any code/rule/regulation which includes text of U.S. statutes/CFR/previously published data must set forth precise identification (titles, dates, editions, page numbers, section numbers, authors), names/addresses of publisher from whom a copy may be obtained, and designated agency offices where material is available for public inspection and copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and effective date; certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No code, rule or regulation is effective until it is filed with the Secretary of State, unless a later date is required by statute. No rule is effective until filed with the Secretary of State and the Notice of Adoption is published in the State Register unless a later date is required by statute, the rule is adopted as an emergency, or it is a '(a)(ii)' rule. Each adopted rule must have a certification attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must cite statutory authority, date of adoption, date of publication in the State Register of the proposed rule making, any other prior publication, and must be signed by the agency head or designated signatory (with written designation on file).

rubrics_metrics.name: NYCRR compilation, style and numbering requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: DOS is responsible for preparing the master compilation of codes, rules and regulations (NYCRR) and may determine form and order. The Secretary of State may advise rulemaking agencies that codes, rules and regulations be uniform in style and form, properly numbered and captioned and be free from obsolete matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must refer to the appropriate Title and to the section or paragraph published in the NYCRR. Agencies must seek approval in writing of proposed title, captions and numbers prior to adoption where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Register publication timing and DOS processing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: DOS publishes all notices and statements required to be in the State Register as soon as practical. The State Register is published each Wednesday. Every notice received in DAR by close of business each Tuesday is published in the weekly issue dated 15 days later. DAR office hours are 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should submit with these timing rules in mind to ensure desired publication week. Non‑compliant notices may be rejected for noncompliance (see notice rejection criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice forms and rejection for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: DOS provides standard rule making notice forms to be used by all agencies. DOS may reject notices that are not in substantial compliance and must give prompt notice of rejection advising the agency of corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DOS‑provided prescribed forms for proposed rule making, notice of adoption, emergency adoption, and combined emergency/proposed forms to avoid rejection.
